evidence._readme: The only TOML client in the registry, which is why it was added: the contract declared TOML as a supported format with no client and no fixtures behind it. Paths and the container shape are CAPTURED from a real installation; the remote-HTTP fields are not, because every server configured on that machine was stdio.

darwin.how: ~/.codex/config.toml read on a real installation (5.2KB) containing live [mcp_servers.*] tables. CODEX_HOME was also observed set in that file's own environment block, which is why codex_home is a base rather than a hardcoded path.

linux.how: Same layout expected via CODEX_HOME or $HOME/.codex; no Linux installation available.

win32.how: No Windows installation available; codex_home has no fallback there, so the location is reported unresolvable rather than guessed.

schema.how: CAPTURED: the container is a TOML table per server, `[mcp_servers.<name>]`, with `command`, `args`, `env`, `cwd`, `enabled` and `startup_timeout_sec` — two real stdio servers were read. DOCUMENTED, NOT observed: the remote-HTTP fields (`url`, headers). No remote server was configured on that machine, so the HTTP shape has not been seen and must be captured before any repair runs.
schema.capture_todo: Add a real remote HTTP MCP server to ~/.codex/config.toml, read back the written table, and confirm the url and header field names before promoting.

repairs.how: No repair round-tripped. TOML repairs additionally need the span-preserving writer proven, exactly as JSONC does.

write_capable._note: All false. The HTTP field names are unconfirmed, so a repair would be guessing at key names in a real developer's file.

locations.note: One file holds everything — model settings, plugins, project trust levels and MCP servers. A repair here sits beside unrelated configuration, which is the strongest possible argument for minimal span edits over reserialising.

server_map._shape_note: TOML tables: [mcp_servers.superdocs]. Note the underscore — not mcpServers, not servers. Three clients, three spellings of the same idea.

transport._note: CAPTURED: entries carrying `command` are stdio — both live servers were of that shape. A remote entry is identified by carrying a URL instead.

headers._accept_note: Field names here are DOCUMENTED, not captured — see evidence.schema. They must be confirmed against a real remote entry before --fix touches this client.

identification._host_rule: Exact host comparison only. Never suffix or substring.

repairs._readme: Empty until the HTTP field names are captured AND a TOML span writer is proven.
repairs._allowed_empty_note: `transport-field` is absent from the plan on purpose: this client has no transport field to repair — remoteness is inferred from the URL.
